title: Microsoft Teams: admin list of custom apps that need updates for private and shared channels
summary: Hold: the app-withdrawal guidance omits Microsoft's requirement to keep blocking settings synchronized across both admin centres until the tenant migrates to unified app management. The roadmap details, manifest guidance, licensing statement and documented Teams paths and command otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Teams admin center lists custom apps in the tenant that need updates to work in private and shared channels.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to view in Teams Admin Center a list of custom apps in their tenant that need to be updated to work in private and shared channels.

claims.claim: The list helps administrators identify impacted apps, understand developer action and coordinate updates.
claims.quote: This experience will help admins identify impacted apps, understand which apps require developer action, and coordinate updates so users can continue using custom apps across all supported channel types.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe the admin list's layout or incompatibility-detection mechanism.

claims.claim: The sources describe no new data access by the list.

claims.claim: Most apps can support shared and private channels with a simple manifest update.
claims.quote: Most apps can support shared and private channels with a simple manifest update.

claims.claim: In manifest v1.25 and later, supportsChannelFeatures replaces supportedChannelTypes.
claims.quote: In app manifest v1.25 and later, use `supportsChannelFeatures` instead of `supportedChannelTypes`.

claims.claim: Apps with none of the four listed membership, file, cross-channel-data or user-type dependencies need only the tier1 declaration and verification and testing across channels.
claims.quote: Then, you only need to: 1. Add `supportsChannelFeatures`: `tier1` to your app manifest 2. Verify expected behavior, and test your app across channels

claims.claim: Apps already published with an earlier manifest version continue to work.
claims.quote: Apps already published with an earlier app manifest version continue to work.

claims.claim: A v1.25-or-later manifest declaring supportedChannelTypes cannot be uploaded or submitted.
claims.quote: In app manifest v1.25 and later, use `supportsChannelFeatures` instead of `supportedChannelTypes`. If your app manifest declares `supportedChannelTypes`, you can't upload or submit your app.

claims.claim: Developers moving their manifest to v1.25 or later must migrate supportedChannelTypes.
claims.quote: Replace `supportedChannelTypes` with `supportsChannelFeatures` when you update your app manifest to v1.25 or later.

claims.quote: If apps are not updated to support private and shared channels, users may be unable to access those app experiences in these channels until the required updates are completed.

claims.claim: Custom apps can be developed within the organisation or commissioned from outside developers.
claims.quote: Your organization can commission the creation of custom apps for your org-specific requirements. Custom apps can be developed within your organization or by app developers outside the organization.

claims.claim: The notice recommends reviewing custom apps used in team and channel scenarios.
claims.quote: Review custom apps used in team and channel scenarios across your organization.

claims.claim: The notice recommends asking developers to complete the required private/shared-channel updates.
claims.quote: Ask your app developers to complete the required updates for private/shared channel scenarios.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice calls for validating updated apps against the scenarios users rely on.
claims.quote: Validate that updated apps continue to support the scenarios your users rely on.

claims.claim: The Manage apps page names Teams Administrator as the role required to use Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Message-extension-only apps operating exclusively in personal scope do not require updates for availability in shared and private channels.
claims.quote: Message extension–only apps that operate exclusively in personal scope do not require updates to be available for users in Shared and Private channels.

claims.claim: An app's details page provides developer contact or website information for support and update enquiries.
claims.quote: For direct support requests and inquiry about agent or app updates, contact the app developer at their website address available at the following two places: • App details page of the app in Manage apps page in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The developer guidance calls for testing the app in standard, private and shared channels.
claims.quote: Test your app in a standard channel, a private channel, and a shared channel.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block is the existing app-state control.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell provides Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> to modify app state.
claims.quote: This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app. Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <String> [-IsBlocked <Boolean>] ... -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Teams Allow or Block control is sufficient to withdraw an app for the organisation, without a qualification about unified app management.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized.
claims.fix: Add to controls[1].note and the After rollout withdrawal bullet: 'Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, keep blocked-app settings synchronized in Teams admin center and under Integrated apps in Microsoft 365 admin center.' This qualification is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-apps#allow-or-block.

claims.claim: The general Allow or Block control does not update the app's private/shared-channel compatibility declaration.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center custom app compatibility list supportsChannelFeatures admin switch automatic action; read manage-apps, all Update-M365TeamsApp parameters and the developer manifest guidance. Blocking controls app state; no manifest compatibility update is documented for it.
